findings.fix: v0.2: a pause is legal only when open_turns==0, and any PromptSubmitted or AgentTurnStarted ends the pause, either as a derived RunResumed or as a fold rule. Agent intervals during a pause should count toward agent_ms and timed_ms, not be removed. Make wall_ms (RTA) the leaderboard key, show timed_ms as personal-only, or cap total pause per run. This is a projection rule change, so it can be applied to old runs by re-folding, but v0.1 PBs should be recomputed and labeled.

critic.reason: projection.rs:491-493 and :531-533 allow turns while paused and pauses with open turns. Clock::new subtracts paused stretches from agent time (projection.rs:171-177), and timed_ms = wall - paused. 'Pause while the agent keeps working' is a natural honest workflow, and it produces false timed and agent numbers on the PB key. It is a fold rule, so re-folding fixes old runs.

findings.title: Verification rules are not part of the versioned category: required evidence is hard-coded by milestone key in the binary, and verifications record no verifier version, so 'rules evolve without invalidating old runs' does not hold
findings.area: category versioning / event model (verify.rs required_kind, category.rs, MilestoneVerified)
findings.evidence: verify.rs:144-152: required_kind matches only the bare key ('deployed', 'legal-pages', 'tests-green', 'first-payment') and ignores category id and version. Job carries key but not category version (service.rs:296-304). The category schema has only a hint, suggested_evidence (category.rs:181-183, 'as a hint'), so a category JSON cannot say that a commit alone is not enough. MilestoneProposed copies title, description and required_trust into the log (service.rs:484-491) but not the evidence requirement, so ARCHITECTURE.md's 'The log is self-contained: it never needs the category file' is false for how a milestone is judged. MilestoneVerified.verifier is just 'git+url' (service.rs:325), with no rule version.
findings.failure_scenario: v0.2 tightens verifiers as A3-1, A3-3 and A3-4 require, for example demanding a url for happy-path-demo or two same-domain legal pages. (1) Runs still open under any-percent@1 or first-revenue@1 are judged by the new code mid-run, although they are pinned to v1. (2) Completed v1 runs verified under the lax rules stay in the same PB pool (category@version) as v1 runs verified under strict rules, so v1 PBs are not comparable. (3) Publishing any-percent@2 with the same keys does not change verification at all unless code is added that branches on version, which nothing passes through. A future cloud verifier cannot tell from the log which rule a MilestoneVerified satisfied.
findings.fix: Move evidence requirements into the category JSON, e.g. `requires: {all_of:["url"], rule:"legal-pages@2"}`. Copy them into MilestoneProposed as an additive field (skip_serializing_if, see A2-5). Dispatch verifiers on (category_id, version, key) via Job. Add `rule_version` to MilestoneVerified. Keep v1 rule implementations frozen for v1 runs, or tag v1 results as 'legacy rules' so they are excluded from leaderboards.

critic.reason: required_kind keys on the bare milestone key only (verify.rs:144-152), and Job carries no category version. This is the structural prerequisite for fixing A3-1, A3-3 and A3-4 without silently changing v1 runs.

findings.title: first-revenue is not 'taken soundly': checkpoints are unordered, so the payment can count before the site, legal pages or tax setup exist, and payments-live and tax are self-declared although Stripe can verify them
findings.evidence: check() allows MilestoneReached on any Accepted milestone at any time (projection.rs:519-522). completion_time is just max(counted_at) over predefined milestones (projection.rs:439-448), and no template field expresses dependencies (category.rs:176-184). Stripe's after_start only compares with run start (verify.rs:701-706), not with when deployed or legal-pages counted. first-revenue.json sets payments-live and tax-compliance to required_trust self_declared with suggested_evidence note only, and auth-and-data-protection to self_declared. The verifier reads a payment's own fields but never the account (charges_enabled or details_submitted) or tax state (automatic_tax on the session or invoice). No amount floor (n('amount_total') > 0, verify.rs:651; captured > 0, :690). No refund or cancellation policy or pricing page milestone.
findings.failure_scenario: The runner sends a Stripe Payment Link to a contact in the first hour, before any product, terms or privacy policy exists, and then deploys a landing page and adds legal pages. The run completes as 'Time to first revenue', dated by the last milestone, and the record says the money was taken compliantly. In fact the customer paid with no terms, no privacy policy and no tax collection. The 'compliance checkpoints' are a checklist that can be ticked afterwards, and three of six can be ticked by the agent alone (A3-5).
findings.fix: first-revenue@2: add `after: ["deployed","legal-pages","payments-live","tax-compliance"]` to first-payment, and have the verifier require payment.created >= those milestones' counted_at. Verify payments-live through GET /v1/account (charges_enabled, details_submitted, and business_profile.url on the deployed domain). Verify tax-compliance through automatic_tax.enabled on the paying session or invoice, or through tax registrations, keeping self_declared plus a note as an explicit lower-trust path. Add a refund/cancellation-policy page to legal-pages and a minimum amount such as 1 USD equivalent. Not verified: the exact Stripe fields, which come from memory of the API.

critic.reason: This is category design, not a bug. Unordered checkpoints are a product choice to make in first-revenue@2. The Stripe field names are from memory.

findings.title: The time-to-first-revenue split is dated when the claim is made, not when the money moved, and no verified fact (amount, currency, paid_at) is kept, so revenue runs cannot be compared, displayed or re-verified off-device
findings.evidence: verify.rs reads created and status_transitions.paid_at (:666-670, :700) only to compare with run start, then discards them. The Outcome has only verifiers and problems (verify.rs:50-62). finish_verification dates MilestoneVerified at job.claimed_at, or at now beyond 10 min (service.rs:316-321), and the split is that time (projection.rs:347-349). ARCHITECTURE.md: 'nothing fetched is stored, only the references the client sent'. Evidence::StripeEvent stores only the id (event.rs:146).
findings.failure_scenario: A customer pays at 10:05 and the agent notices and claims at 16:40, or the claim is spooled: the 'time to first revenue' is 6.5 h too long. The reverse case is that the result shows nothing about what was earned, so a $0.50 test purchase and a $500 sale look the same on a PB or leaderboard. A future sync server cannot re-check the payment without the user's Stripe secret, so cloud results must trust the device's 'stripe' verifier string entirely.
findings.fix: Add an additive `observed` object to MilestoneVerified, e.g. {paid_at, amount, currency, object_id, livemode} for Stripe, {completed_at, head_sha, workflow_path} for CI, and {fetched_at, final_url, status} for URLs. For first-payment, date the split at paid_at, clamped to [run start, claim time]. Show amount and currency in LiveMilestone. Decide now whether leaderboards need a server-side check (e.g. Stripe Connect read access) and design the evidence shape for it.

critic.reason: The split is dated at the claim (service.rs:316-321), and paid_at is discarded. This is a design improvement for revenue runs, not a v0.1 defect.

findings.title: Agent-generated milestones are decorative and the human cannot complete them: they are fixed at agent_claimed, the user's own `speedrun split` never counts for them, and they have no link to the prompt they were derived from or any comparable identity
findings.area: milestone flow (tools.rs propose, main.rs Add/Split, live.rs PB splits)
findings.evidence: tools.rs:88-92: every agent proposal gets key None and required_trust AgentClaimed, and the user cannot change either (accept takes no options, main.rs Accept). main.rs:279-282: the user's split always claims Trust::SelfDeclared, which is below AgentClaimed (event.rs:132-137), so counts() (projection.rs:69-72) is false when the user marks an agent milestone done without verifiable evidence. Only the agent's own claim satisfies it. Completion considers only Predefined milestones (projection.rs:429-436), so accepted agent and user milestones never define when a run is finished. pb_split is computed only for Predefined with a key (live.rs:127-142). MilestoneProposed has no reference to the initial prompt or goal (event.rs:56-64), and the propose tool can be called at any point in the run, so 'derived from the initial prompt' is neither recorded nor enforced.
findings.failure_scenario: The user starts a run, the agent proposes 5 project-specific milestones and the user accepts them. The user does a step themselves and runs `speedrun split <id>`, and status shows it as reached but not counting ('◐'), permanently. Meanwhile the agent can mark any of them done on its own word. The milestones the original intent asked for (user-entered or agent-generated from the prompt) never affect the finish line, carry no splits comparable across runs, and cannot be traced back to the goal they were derived from.
findings.fix: v0.2: add additive fields to MilestoneProposed: `derived_from` (prompt event_id), suggested_evidence, and an optional stable slug. Let accept set required_trust and required evidence. Separate claimant (user|agent) from trust strength (see A3-5) so a user claim counts for a user-confirmed milestone. Add a `custom` category, or a per-run 'goal set' frozen at accept time, in which the accepted agent and user milestones are the finish line. Mark such runs as not leaderboard-comparable.

critic.reason: tools.rs:92 fixes required_trust at AgentClaimed, and main.rs:279-282 always claims SelfDeclared, so the user's own split never counts for an agent milestone. This user-facing flow is visibly broken on first use.

findings.title: PBs are not comparable: the PB is the fastest run of the category in any project, and every category version bump (which the v0.2 verifier fixes need) silently moves new runs to an empty PB pool
findings.evidence: service.rs:410-428 selects PBs from reader.runs_in_category(category_id, version), across all projects, sorted by timed_ms. live.rs:48 describes it as 'Best earlier completed run of the same category and version'. Nothing records what was built: no goal, prompt-derived task or seed (event.rs:35-40). project.json stores only category_id, with no version (project.rs:12-16), and a new run takes the newest built-in version (service.rs:121, category::find(.., None)). CLAUDE.md requires changing categories by adding versions.
findings.failure_scenario: A user's 40-minute any% for a CLI todo tool becomes the PB shown with a red delta on every later any% run, including a 2-day multiplayer game, so the deltas mean nothing. When v0.2 adds any-percent@2 to close A3-1, the binary upgrade moves the next run in every project to @2 without saying so, and all PBs and per-split deltas vanish. Leaderboards inherit both problems: rankings across unrelated products, and a split at each rules version.
findings.fix: Scope PBs to the project by default (same project_id), with category-wide as an option. Record a goal or seed on RunStarted (additive), from the initial prompt summary or a user-chosen 'challenge' id, so public boards can compare like with like. Pin category_version in project.json at init and make upgrades explicit (`speedrun init --upgrade-category`). Add category metadata such as `comparable_with: [1]` for versions that only tighten verification.

critic.reason: completed_runs (service.rs:409-428) selects across all projects for a category@version, so PB deltas compare unrelated products. project.json does not pin the category version. The auditor's version-bump point is valid and matters for v0.2 planning.

findings.title: The chain hash commits to plaintext prompt text, so the planned timing-only sync and prompt encryption at rest cannot coexist with chain verification for any v0.1 event
findings.area: data model / cloud sync and privacy roadmap (hash.rs, PromptSubmitted)
findings.evidence: hash.rs:45-51 hashes the whole serialized Event, including payload.content of PromptSubmitted (event.rs:41-49). ARCHITECTURE.md Privacy: 'Planned: encrypt prompt content at rest ... Make syncing prompt text opt-in and separate from syncing timing metadata'. Roadmap item 3: 'verify chains server-side'. Payloads are immutable once written (CLAUDE.md).
findings.failure_scenario: v0.3 ships sync without prompt text, as promised. The server receives PromptSubmitted events with content stripped, cannot recompute any hash from that seq onward, and therefore cannot verify any run's chain. That defeats server-side chain verification and leaderboard eligibility for all v0.1/v0.2 history, unless users upload every prompt. Likewise, encrypting content in place at rest changes the stored body and breaks verify_chain (made worse by A2-5's re-serialization). Every run recorded from v0.1 on is locked into one of these choices, and it gets more expensive with every release that keeps the format.
findings.fix: Fix it in v0.2 before sync: PromptSubmitted v2 (SCHEMA_VERSION bump) carries `content_digest` = HMAC-SHA256(per-device secret, content) plus length and redacted. The text goes in a separate prompts table keyed by event_id, outside the chain, where it can be encrypted or synced on its own. Use a salted or keyed hash because short prompts are guessable. Old v0.1 events stay verifiable only locally or with their text, and the docs should say so.

critic.reason: compute_hash covers the whole payload, including the prompt content. Encryption at rest or timing-only sync would break the chain, and this design decision must be made before more data accumulates. It is a roadmap constraint, not a v0.1 bug.

findings.title: Run and milestone identity is single-device and single-category, which blocks the roadmap's sync (one project on two machines) and its 'any% inside 100% inside first revenue' timeline
findings.area: data model / sync readiness (store.rs chain, service.rs start_run, project.rs)
findings.evidence: Each run is one gapless seq plus prev_hash chain written by one daemon (event.rs:18-27, ARCHITECTURE.md Event log), and run_id is minted locally at the first prompt (service.rs:466). project_id is committed so that it is 'stable across clones and machines' (project.rs:9-10), and latest_run(project_id) decides which run receives prompts (service.rs:114-119). Predefined milestone_id equals the bare key (service.rs:481-485). any-percent and hundred-percent both use 'scaffold-runs' and 'happy-path-demo', with different descriptions ('Stubs and fakes are allowed' only in any%).
findings.failure_scenario: A user works on the same repo from a laptop and a desktop. Each daemon starts its own run for the same project_id, and after sync the server has two concurrent 'latest' runs with independent chains and no way to merge them, so the 'run' is split across two partial timelines. Forks and clones of a public repo share the committed project_id, so different people's runs look like one project. Multi-category runs (roadmap 4) cannot hold any% and 100% 'happy-path-demo' at once because milestone_id is the bare key, and existing v0.1 events already use that id.
findings.fix: Before v0.2 freezes more data: namespace predefined ids as `<category>@<version>/<key>` in new runs, keeping fold reading bare keys. Decide the multi-device model now. Either runs belong to one device and the server picks or merges per project explicitly, or chains become per (run, device) with a run-level merge order defined by the server. Record device/account ownership in RunStarted. Detect forks by storing the repo's root commit in project.json, and give a fork a new project_id on `speedrun init`.

critic.reason: Design analysis against a sync feature that does not exist yet. Namespacing predefined ids is cheap to do now. The rest is speculative.

findings.title: The live-display contract is not ready for remote clients: no protocol version, a cursor only meaningful within one local DB, no source identity, and a documented 'abandoned' status that never appears
findings.evidence: LiveSnapshot has only as_of, cursor and runs (live.rs:16-24). LIVE_DISPLAY.md 'Compatibility' promises 'a protocol version bump', but no version field exists in the snapshot or in /v1/health's {ok, version} (http.rs:110). cursor = MAX(rowid) of the local events table (store.rs:149-155), and displays are told to 'Drop any snapshot whose cursor is lower' while treating the transport as swappable (local SSE, cloud, static file). Service::live drops closed runs (service.rs:392), so status 'abandoned', listed in the contract, is never sent. LiveMilestone carries no description, evidence summary or counted_at timestamp, so a display cannot show what a split was or animate 'just split' without diffing.
findings.failure_scenario: A phone or PiP client built from another team's design system follows the contract. It shows local SSE (cursor 9,812), then switches to the cloud source, whose cursor space starts lower, or the local DB is restored or the data dir changes (A5-3). It then drops every new snapshot as stale and freezes with no error. When v0.2 changes a field's meaning, as several fixes above require, existing widgets cannot detect the version and render wrong clocks.
findings.fix: Add `protocol: 1` and `source: {kind: local|cloud, id: device_or_account}` to LiveSnapshot. Define the cursor as comparable only within one source, and require clients to reset when the source changes. Add counted_at, description and a short evidence summary to LiveMilestone. Either stop listing 'abandoned' or show recently abandoned runs. Generate and publish a versioned TS/Swift package from the schema so design-system teams do not hand-copy types.

critic.reason: LiveSnapshot has no protocol version, and 'abandoned' is never emitted because closed runs are filtered out (service.rs:390-392). Fix the contract now; nothing breaks for local-only v0.1.

critic_missed: crates/speedrun-cli/src/client.rs:110-112 + :214-258: every hook (Client::new, 5 s timeout, hook.rs:62/104) calls ready(), which synchronously flushes the whole spool before it records the fresh event. Each spooled POST can take up to 5 s, and the Claude Code hook timeout is 10 s (hooks.json). A backlog of 2 or more slow items therefore gets the hook killed mid-flush. The fresh prompt is never recorded, and the claimed flushing-*.jsonl file is only picked up again after the 120 s staleness window (:224). Reasoned from code, not reproduced.

crates/speedrun-cli/src/client.rs:104 + :244-249 with service.rs:233: a ureq timeout is a Transport error, which maps to CallError::Unreachable. A spooled MilestoneReached whose replay triggers network verification (up to 15 s, verify.rs) exceeds the 5 s hook client timeout and is re-spooled as 'unreachable', even though the daemon finished the work. Retried claims 're-check evidence' (service.rs:233), so every later hook pays the full 5 s timeout again, and the entry can loop in the spool. Not reproduced.

crates/speedrun-core/src/event.rs (no skip_serializing_if on any payload field; only api.rs:67 has one) + hash.rs:45-51: the 'additive changes keep the version' rule (ARCHITECTURE.md:43) cannot be followed today without breaking verify_chain for all history. A regression fixture of a frozen v0.1 DB should be added before any v0.2 schema edit. Relates to A2-5, whose line citations are wrong (hash.rs has 162 lines; verify_chain is at :70).

.github/workflows/release.yml: no job runs `cargo test`/clippy on the workspace (the only cargo test is the Zed one at :91). Together with A4-1 and the marketplace plugin tracking main, a hooks.json change merged to main reaches users immediately, without a release and without any compatibility test against the last released binary.

disputes.reason: The '0755 spool dir' point is weaker than stated. The spool dir sits inside the data dir, and speedrund sets the data dir to 0700 on every start (crates/speedrund/src/main.rs:48-49), so other users cannot traverse into spool/ once the daemon has run, whatever the spool dir's own mode is. The exposure is real only when the daemon never started (SPEEDRUN_NO_AUTOSTART, or a missing binary) and the client's create_dir_all (client.rs:272, :296) made the data dir with the umask default. The plaintext-in-rejected.jsonl point stands.

Backdating a RunPaused zeroes timed_ms for whole runs in every category, evidence_verified splits included, and timed_ms is the PB ranking key (service.rs:423). Pause intervals use the client's occurred_at, raised only to run start (projection.rs:267, :361-371), and clamp_time has no lower bound (service.rs:60-63). VERIFIED with the temp daemon: POST /v1/projects/<id>/events with {type:'run_paused'} and occurred_at=<run started_at}, then run_resumed, then claims. The run completed with 'timed 0:00:00 agent 0:00:00' while real time was 0:00:04. Agent time inside the pause is subtracted too (projection.rs:175-177). The fix must also bound RunPaused and RunResumed times from below.

The issue applies to Claude Code and Copilot only. opencode ends turns on session.status idle and session.idle, which fire on abort too (plugins/opencode/agentspeedrun.ts:129-132). pi ends turns on agent_end and session_shutdown (plugins/pi/agentspeedrun.ts:135-151). The Claude Code docs list StopFailure among the per-turn events ('per turn: UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and StopFailure') with output ignored, so hooking it is safe, and the plugin does not. For Copilot, the CLI reference documents agentStop only as 'the main agent finishes a turn'. Its sessionEnd has a reason 'abort', and hook.rs:78 maps session-end to a turn end only at session close. A second, separate path also inflates or deflates agent time (see my Stop-block finding): a Stop that another hook blocks ends the turn early.

'Tag builds restore rust-cache caches written by main pushes' is overstated for the published binaries. Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 includes the job id ($GITHUB_JOB) in its cache key by default. The release `binaries` job (key = matrix.target) shares no job id with any ci.yml job (rust, adapters, vscode, zed, package), so main-push CI caches cannot be restored into the job that builds the published tarballs. The caches it can restore come from earlier release runs of the same job, including workflow_dispatch dry runs on main (release.yml:7). Release `vscode` does share the job id 'vscode' with ci.yml and has no key, so it can restore ci's main cache, but that cache only holds the debug cargo build used for tests, not the .vsix contents. The supply-chain point about mutable action tags and unpinned cargo-zigbuild still stands. Reasoned from rust-cache's documented key scheme; not checked against a live Actions cache listing.

The silent-401 loss does not need a race. Any persistent mismatch between the client's data dir and the running daemon's data dir causes it, because the address is global (paths.rs:4) while the token lives in the data dir. VERIFIED with daemon A on homeA and a hook with SPEEDRUN_HOME=homeB on the same port: the hook printed 'speedrund error 401', exited 0 and spooled nothing. The failed autostart had already written a token, display-token and a fresh speedrun.sqlite into homeB before failing to bind (main.rs:50-53 vs :62), so the mismatch then persists. This is reachable on Linux whenever XDG_DATA_HOME differs between the terminal and the GUI-launched editor environments (see my data-dir finding).

For the second, legitimate user on a shared host, the consequence is silent data loss, not just 'cannot run a daemon'. Their hooks reach user A's real speedrund (health is unauthenticated), send their own token, get 401 (not spooled, client.rs:133-139), and exit 0. I reproduced the same mechanism with two data dirs on one port.

The proposed fix, 'Publish new category versions in which a commit alone cannot satisfy evidence_verified', cannot be done through category JSON. Required evidence is hard-coded by bare key in verify.rs:144-152, with no category version in Job (service.rs:296-304), and the category schema has only a suggested_evidence hint (category.rs:181-183). A new any-percent@2 with the same keys gets exactly the v1 verification unless verifier dispatch gains a version. Code changes that tighten 'happy-path-demo' would also apply mid-run to open @1 runs.

The trust ordering also stops the human from completing agent-proposed milestones. tools.rs:92 fixes their required_trust at AgentClaimed, while `speedrun split` always claims SelfDeclared (main.rs:279-282), so a user's split of an accepted agent milestone never counts. Only the agent can satisfy it on its own word. Provenance is inverted in both directions.

Besides additive fields, the roadmap's prompt encryption at rest and timing-only sync both change or remove payload.content. The hash covers it (hash.rs:45-51 over the full Event), so either feature breaks verify_chain for every v0.1 run. Hashing the stored body does not fix this. A content digest separate from the text is needed (see the hash-commits-to-plaintext finding).

gaps:
security: Checked and found sound, by code reading plus a live temp daemon on 127.0.0.1:34571:
- Route coverage: every route except /v1/health is behind auth or display_auth (http.rs:84-114).
- Token handling: tokens are compared in constant time. They come from two ULIDs (Ulid::new uses thread_rng; 160 random bits). Token files are 0600 and the data dir is chmod 0700 at daemon start.
- Display token scope: it got 401 on /v1/runs/*. LiveRun/LiveMilestone carry no prompt or evidence fields.
- CORS: it is applied only to the display router, GET only.
- DNS rebinding: Host is not validated, but every data route needs a bearer token, so a rebinding page only reaches /v1/health.
- Non-loopback guard: binding outside loopback is refused unless SPEEDRUN_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK is set (main.rs:357). Any value, even 0, enables it; that is minor.
- API credentials: the API agent has redirects(0). GitHub and Stripe credentials only go to fixed hosts (api.github.com, api.stripe.com). Stripe ids and GitHub owner/repo/run id are strictly validated, including ids chained from Stripe responses.
- Git argument injection: git SHAs (including GitHub's head_sha) are hex-validated before any git call, so no argument injection.
- Page fetches: redirects are re-resolved through the filtering resolver and https_only is enforced.
- Secrets: `speedrun secret set` writes 0600 files into a 0700 dir via atomic rename.

Not done:
- No real SSRF probing against NAT64 or a proxy.
- No check of whether a malicious repo's .git/config (e.g. log.showSignature + gpg.program) can make the daemon's `git -C project_root log` run a command. That only matters for repos that ship their own .git dir (archives, embedded bare repos).
- The VS Code, Zed, opencode and pi adapters were not audited beyond confirming VS Code uses `speedrun display --json` (the display token).
- No check of MCP stdin parsing robustness.
- ARCHITECTURE's trust model is not treated as a finding: the timed agent runs as the same user and can read $SPEEDRUN_HOME/token, so it can forge self-declared events by design.
